## memory.toml


Located at `/Users/arka/.config/agentic-memory/memory.toml`:


```toml

# Agentic Memory configuration
# Every field here can be overridden by the corresponding MEMORY_* env var.
# Env var precedence: MEMORY_<FIELD> > memory.toml > code defaults.

[general]
db_path = "memory/memory.db"          # MEMORY_DB_PATH
wal_checkpoint_startup = true          # MEMORY_WAL_CHECKPOINT_STARTUP — run a WAL checkpoint on startup to keep memory.db-wal small
wal_checkpoint_interval_s = 300         # MEMORY_WAL_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_S — periodic debounced WAL checkpoint inside background_worker (S4.5, 2026-06-23). 0 to disable.
mmap_size = 268435456                  # MEMORY_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE — SQLite mmap_size in BYTES (S4.1, 2026-06-23). Default 256 MiB. Set to 0 to disable mmap. See docs/perf.md for tradeoffs.
unindexed_safety_net_limit = 1000     # MEMORY_UNINDEXED_SAFETY_NET_LIMIT
db_pool_size = 24                      # MEMORY_DB_POOL_SIZE — max concurrent SQLite connections
agent_id = ""                          # MEMORY_AGENT_ID — CRDT agent identifier (auto-detected from hostname if empty)

[search]
temporal_half_life = 180              # MEMORY_TEMPORAL_HALF_LIFE
temporal_decay_mode = "exponential"   # MEMORY_TEMPORAL_DECAY_MODE
late_interaction = true               # MEMORY_LATE_INTERACTION
knowledge_graph = true                # MEMORY_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH
graph_rag_hops = 3                    # MEMORY_GRAPH_RAG_HOPS
graph_rag_expansions = 5              # MEMORY_GRAPH_RAG_EXPANSIONS
query_cache = true                    # MEMORY_QUERY_CACHE
search_parallel_enabled = true        # MEMORY_SEARCH_PARALLEL — run FTS + KG fact search in parallel when both are requested
reranker_disabled = false             # MEMORY_RERANKER_DISABLED — Qwen3-0.6B primary, BGE-m3 fallback (both MPS-safe, verified 2026-06-15). Set to true to disable.
deep_rerank_timeout = 30              # MEMORY_DEEP_RERANK_TIMEOUT — wall-clock seconds before the deep reranker subprocess is killed (2026-06-19 MPS hang insurance). Set to 0 to disable the timeout (run in-process, fast but no kill switch on hang).
contextual_retrieval = true           # MEMORY_CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL — prepend category+tags context to embeddings
contextual_enrichment = true          # MEMORY_CONTEXTUAL_ENRICHMENT
forgetting_curve = true               # MEMORY_FORGETTING_CURVE — Ebbinghaus decay boosts recent notes
forgetting_curve_half_life = 30       # MEMORY_FORGETTING_CURVE_HALF_LIFE — Ebbinghaus half-life in DAYS (float, e.g. 30 or 7.5). Used by neural_forget.py and the search scoring pipeline.
vec_rebuild_threshold = 15           # MEMORY_VEC_REBUILD_THRESHOLD — count of drift rows (vec_keys/embeddings mismatch) that triggers an automatic vec index rebuild. Default 15 (was 5, raised 2026-06-23) tolerates single-row drift without forcing a rebuild. Set to 0 to disable auto-rebuild, or 100+ to make it very lazy (drift will accumulate).
vec_rebuild_adaptive = true          # MEMORY_VEC_REBUILD_ADAPTIVE — scale threshold dynamically based on write velocity. Threshold = base * clamp(drift_rate / velocity, 0.5, 3.0).
concept_drift_threshold = 0.15       # MEMORY_CONCEPT_DRIFT_THRESHOLD — cosine drift threshold for concept drift cron
entity_min_occurrences = 2           # MEMORY_ENTITY_MIN_OCCURRENCES — min occurrences for regex entity extraction (tight=2, legacy=1)
ctr_data_window_days = 90            # MEMORY_CTR_DATA_WINDOW_DAYS — CTR feedback lookback window

# Rerank channel weights (JSON). Override via MEMORY_RERANK_WEIGHTS env var.
# Empty string (default) falls back to built-in weights below.
# Keys: bm25, fitness, importance, pinned, tag_match — must sum to 1.0.
rerank_weights = ""                           # MEMORY_RERANK_WEIGHTS

# Rerank / blend / threshold tunables (P3-32)
rerank_half_life_days = 180          # MEMORY_RERANK_HALF_LIFE_DAYS
cross_encoder_blend = 0.6            # MEMORY_CROSS_ENCODER_BLEND
late_interaction_blend = 0.3         # MEMORY_LATE_INTERACTION_BLEND
topic_similarity_threshold = 0.15    # MEMORY_TOPIC_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
temporal_decay_weight = 0.15         # MEMORY_TEMPORAL_DECAY_WEIGHT
ce_blend = 0.85                       # MEMORY_CE_BLEND — PR1.2 single-CE blend (weak/chunk/deep all use this)
ce_chunk_blend = 0.7                   # MEMORY_CE_CHUNK_BLEND — PR1.2 chunk-CE blend (matches PR1.1-validated full pipeline; weak/deep use ce_blend=0.85)
ce_deep_enabled = false              # MEMORY_CE_DEEP — gate deep (Qwen3) CE on env MEMORY_CE_DEEP=1
colbert_enabled = true               # MEMORY_COLBERT_ENABLED — enable ColBERT MaxSim reranking (Phase 3)
colbert_model = ""                   # MEMORY_COLBERT_MODEL — ColBERT model name (default: colbert-ir/colbertv2.0)
colbert_blend = 0.4                  # MEMORY_COLBERT_BLEND — ColBERT score weight in final blend
colbert_max_candidates = 30          # MEMORY_COLBERT_MAX_CANDIDATES — skip reranking when candidates exceed this
colbert_min_query_tokens = 3         # MEMORY_COLBERT_MIN_QUERY_TOKENS — skip reranking for shorter queries
splade_enabled = true                # MEMORY_SPLADE_ENABLED — enable SPLADE sparse recall (Phase 4)
splade_model = ""                    # MEMORY_SPLADE_MODEL — SPLADE model name (default: naver/splade-cocondenser-ensembledistil)
hybrid_splade_weight = 0.6           # MEMORY_HYBRID_SPLADE_WEIGHT — SPLADE weight in RRF fusion
answer_rerank_blend = 0.3            # MEMORY_ANSWER_RERANK_BLEND — answer snippet score weight in final blend
answer_rerank_enabled = true         # MEMORY_ANSWER_RERANK_ENABLED — enable answer-level reranking (Phase 5)
ctr_weight_learning = true           # MEMORY_CTR_WEIGHT_LEARNING — enable per-query-type CTR weight learning (Phase 6)
ctr_min_interactions = 10            # MEMORY_CTR_MIN_INTERACTIONS — min interactions per query type for learning
search_compute_budget_ms = 0         # MEMORY_SEARCH_COMPUTE_BUDGET_MS — max ms for search (0=unlimited). <50 skips CE, <100 skips chunk CE, <300 skips ColBERT+answer rerank. Set to 0 for unlimited (full pipeline). Override with env MEMORY_SEARCH_COMPUTE_BUDGET_MS=0 for unlimited.

[features]
# All features on by default so the agent gets the richest possible
# context automatically. Set any to false to opt out.
write_journal = true                    # MEMORY_WRITE_JOURNAL_ENABLED — CQRS write journal (lock-free multi-writer). Requires background_worker daemon.
write_journal_fallback_sync = true      # MEMORY_WRITE_JOURNAL_FALLBACK_SYNC — when the journal backlog is full, fall back to synchronous save_memory instead of raising.
multi_agent = true                    # MEMORY_MULTI_AGENT — cross-agent memory sharing via shared_memories table
summarization = true                  # MEMORY_SUMMARIZATION — auto-summarize long notes via TF-IDF
user_profile = true                   # MEMORY_USER_PROFILE — personalize recall ranking from access history
self_directed = true                  # MEMORY_SELF_DIRECTED — self-healing: heartbeat, tier assignment, archive
adaptive_retention = true             # MEMORY_ADAPTIVE_RETENTION — psi formula + spaced repetition
neural_forget_mode = "learned"        # MEMORY_NEURAL_FORGET_MODE — "formula" | "learned" | "hybrid"; falls back to formula until trained
temporal_ssm_enabled = true           # MEMORY_TEMPORAL_SSM_ENABLED — opt-in; trained weekly by cron/cron_train_temporal_ssm.py. Neutral (no ranking effect) until a checkpoint is written.
consolidation = true                  # MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION — SHA-256 + n-gram Jaccard dedup, contradiction scan
quality_gates = true                  # MEMORY_QUALITY_GATES — filter results below relevance threshold
```

## Priority Order

1. Environment variables (highest priority)
2. `memory.toml` file
3. Default values (lowest priority)

## Configuration Examples

### Minimal Setup

```bash
# Just FTS5 search, no extras
export MEMORY_DB_PATH=/data/memory.db
```

### Full-Featured Setup

```bash
# Everything enabled
export MEMORY_MULTI_AGENT=1
export MEMORY_CRDT_ENABLED=1
export MEMORY_SYNC_ENABLE_SERVER=1
export MEMORY_SYNC_LISTEN_PORT=9877
```

### Multi-Agent Peer Sync

```bash
export MEMORY_DB_PATH=/data/agent-a/memory.db
export MEMORY_AGENT_ID=agent-a
export MEMORY_SYNC_ENABLE_SERVER=1
export MEMORY_SYNC_LISTEN_PORT=9877
export MEMORY_MULTI_AGENT=1
```

## mmap tradeoffs

**S4.10 (2026-06-23):** the `mmap_size` PRAGMA tells SQLite to memory-map the DB file directly into the process address space, bypassing the `read()` syscall on the hot path. Default is 256 MiB.

**Pros** (measured 2026-06-23 on a 200K-row test DB with cold cache):
- ~10–14% read speedup vs no-mmap (1.70 μs → 1.70 μs warm, 2.81 μs → 2.47 μs cold).
- Eliminates one copy on the read path (kernel → user).
- Pages are demand-loaded — unused regions of the DB don't consume RAM.
- Survives `process restart` (no re-read of cached pages).

**Cons**:
- A `SIGBUS` on the mmap'd file (e.g. an external `truncate` while the DB is open) will crash the process. SQLite normally holds a `fcntl` lock that prevents this; if you run `sqlite3` against the same DB while the agent is running, you can hit it.
- Reading from mmap on macOS sometimes touches the unified-memory allocator. Not a problem in practice (256 MiB is rounding error on a 16 GiB system), but on a 4 GiB laptop the kernel may evict other pages.
- The mmap doesn't include the WAL — only the main DB file. So write-heavy workloads see no benefit.

**When to disable** (`MEMORY_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE=0`):
- DB > 50% of available RAM.
- You're running multiple agents against the same DB and want to avoid address-space duplication.
- You're debugging a `SIGBUS` and want to rule out mmap.

**When to keep at default** (256 MiB):
- Single-agent, DB < 1 GiB, plenty of RAM. This is the common case.
